title: Necessity Conditions for Identification under Selection Bias with External Margins
banked_reason: Sound scoped results, but no theorem turns every terminal EXT-ID failure into a same-input separating pair; achieved subfield ceiling 6.8 below the field floor.
proof_attempt_summary: The run built a finite terminating EXT-ID transition system, proved success soundness, a conditional projective nullspace certificate, an exact three-node rational witness, fixed-fiber semialgebraic characterization, and boundary obstruction results. The field-level step collapsed because neither the projective argument nor the available quantifier-elimination substrate derives a feasible same-input separating pair from every terminal EXT-ID failure. A future revival must prove the margin-anchored hedge or add a genuinely complete recovery rule, while also supplying a sourced finite-disturbance full-law reduction.
tldr: The achieved headline is a graph-level necessity result on the terminal-unconfounded selection subclass, not universal completeness of EXT-ID. If a causal cell is not identifiable from a strictly positive full observational law on the substantive ADMG \(\mathcal G[V]\), Kivva et al.'s positive ordinary-ID specialization supplies two positive finite models with the same \(P(V)\) and different intervention cells. Extending both by any common strictly positive terminal selection kernel preserves the same normalized selected law \(q_S=P(V\mid S=1)\), every external margin \(q_0=P(T_0)\), and the causal disagreement in one exact \(\epsilon\)-positive fiber. Hence recovery from the two laws on this subclass requires ordinary positive-model identification. At \(T_0=V\), this converse combines with the boundary reduction to give an exact equivalence, and EXT-ID succeeds for every ordinarily identifiable positive-model cell. The general algebraic SCM class remains broader than the terminal-sink subclass; successful EXT-ID formulas are sound and the procedure terminates, but a bare EXT-ID failure is not a universal nonidentification certificate. The projective null-space theorem and canonical response-fiber characterization remain conditional and fixed-fiber supporting results.
gap: Correa, Tian, and Bareinboim define the exact two-law problem and prove IDSB sound but leave completeness unclear. Tikka, Hyttinen, and Karvanen can express both sources in do-search, but their Theorem 3 negative-answer guarantee covers Table 1 Rows 1--4 and 6 rather than generalized identifiability in Row 8, whose completeness is listed as unknown. Qiu et al. give a probability-class iff for scalar ATE with an unbiased covariate margin, not arbitrary finite-state semi-Markovian ADMG queries.
fill: The project defines the model-induced observation map, its exact compatible image, and each observed-data fiber; gives an exact source-tagged transition relation over a bounded graph-indexed inventory; and supplies a representation-indexed projective obstruction whose coordinates are exactly the chosen response variable's positive support and whose perturbation has a valid input-specific interior bound. A named three-node exact-fiber witness is the first gate; a parameterized real-closed-field elimination and cylindrical-algebraic partition over symbolic observed tables is the second; and the universal margin-anchored hedge is the focal open theorem. Completeness is only the integration corollary after these ordered gates are discharged.
